questions.q: Why are brands like Crumbl, Dave's Hot Chicken and 7 Brew growing so fast?
questions.a: These brands combine a focused menu, careful franchising, strong digital culture and loyalty systems built into the business. Each one is built around one hero product category, which keeps operations simple and consistent. Their social media presence and apps turn first-time buyers into regulars.

questions.q: Why does a simple menu help a restaurant chain scale?
questions.a: A short, focused menu makes training and staffing faster, needs smaller kitchens and lowers overhead. It also keeps quality more consistent across locations and gives you a clearer story to tell online. Bloated menus add back-of-house complexity that slows growth.

questions.q: How do viral QSR brands use social media?
questions.a: They create moments people want to share, such as limited-time flavor drops, eye-catching packaging and a lively crew culture. They also treat social channels as a feedback loop, listening to guests and adapting quickly. That kind of cultural pull is hard to buy with ads alone.

questions.q: How important is a loyalty program for QSR growth?
questions.a: Loyalty works best when you treat it as a core platform for the business. Apps, rewards, sneak peeks and social-only offers create habits that bring guests back each week. New customers may find you on social media, while good systems are what keep them coming back.

questions.q: What can legacy QSR brands learn from these fast-growing chains?
questions.a: Start by auditing your menu to see whether it helps you scale or slows you down. Invest in owned channels like loyalty, SMS and your app, and look for ways to simplify the store. It's also worth asking whether anyone would share your product online without being paid.
